Five thousand years ago, two armies stood face to face, on a field called Kurukshetra.
And the greatest archer alive... let his bow fall.
My limbs are failing. My mouth is dry. Gandiva slips from my hand. I will not fight, Krishna.
Krishna did not argue. He smiled... and he spoke.
क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ। उत्तिष्ठ परन्तप।
Do not yield to this weakness, Partha. It does not become you. Stand up.
You grieve for what cannot die. Weapons cannot cut the soul. Fire cannot burn it. It was never born. It will never die.
Your right is to the work alone. Never to its fruits. Act... and let the outcome go.
Whenever dharma fades, and wrong rises... I come. Age after age.
Then Arjuna asked to see him as he truly is.
I am Time. The mighty destroyer of worlds.
If a thousand suns rose at once in the sky, that would be the splendour of that mighty being.
Let go of everything, and come to me. I will free you. Do not grieve.
My delusion is gone. My doubts are gone. I will do as you say.
The Bhagavad Gita. Seven hundred verses. One conversation. Still speaking.
